title: RAFT: Part 3 - Outperforming Llama 3 & GPT-4 on Medical and Code Tasks

beats.text: Why are leading AI teams switching to RAFT after this 98.2% benchmark result?
beats.visual_focus: A glowing query vector enters a vector database and retrieves four documents, three of which glow red with toxic noise.

beats.text: Standard RAG injects top search snippets into prompts. But when irrelevant distractor texts sneak in. Models fixate on false clues.
beats.visual_focus: Transformer attention map spreading probability weights across junk documents instead of the one correct medical paragraph.

beats.text: Researchers created RAFT. Retrieval Augmented Fine-Tuning. Instead of assuming perfect inputs. They intentionally train models on noisy document batches.
beats.visual_focus: Chalkboard training pipeline showing training instances populated with curated target answers alongside adversarial distractor documents.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: This is genuinely great. The hook stopped me immediately because everyone tells you RAG stops hallucinations, so hearing that it actually makes them worse grabs attention right away. You explained the actual fix cleanly without making up dumb metaphors like 'filing cabinets'—training models on intentional distractor batches makes total sense. Naming Gorilla and PubMed in Beat 5 grounded it in real benchmarks instead of vague hype.
